page: Amazon Web Services m8id.32xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. This x86_64 architecture system features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes 480 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for vector and matrix operations. Memory configuration consists of 512.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core.

The instance is equipped with 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volumes, offering high-capacity, low-latency local storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. The system does not include any GPU hardware.

Benchmark results place the m8id.32xlarge in the top tier for multi-core processing and memory performance. The system achieved a multi-core stress-ng score of 138,373.51 and a Passmark CPU score of 122,861.45. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 10,210.31 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 392.68 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database operations are highly efficient, with a Passmark database score of 34,690.7 and Redis SET operations reaching 210.58 million operations per second. In LLM inference, the server demonstrates top-tier prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large models, though text generation speeds for smaller models scale down to average levels.

Given its high resource density, including DDR5 memory and 7.6 TB of local NVMe storage, the server offers a balanced cost-to-performance profile for resource-intensive workloads. The combination of high-speed memory, dedicated compute cores, and substantial local storage makes this instance suitable for large-scale databases, software compilation, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
